h2: Turnaround inspection services: what the NDE contractor brings to the outage
html:
Owners buying turnaround services want the inspection scope finished inside the outage window without it becoming the critical path. The NDE contractor's job is to arrive with the scope already planned, staff every method the work list needs, report daily, and absorb the emergent work that opening equipment always produces.

Before the outage

Turnaround inspection services start months earlier, from the owner's inspection plans: the API 510 and API 570 work lists, the exchanger bundles to be pulled, the vessels to be entered and the piping circuits that are due. We turn that list into a method-by-item scope, confirm the procedures and the certification each method needs, and agree the access each item depends on: scaffold, insulation removal, cleaning, blinding and entry permits. Most delays at the inspection step trace back to access that was assumed rather than planned.

During the outage

Typical shutdown inspection work covers internal visual examination of vessels, UT thickness at condition monitoring locations, corrosion mapping of known damage, wet fluorescent magnetic particle inspection of welds in cracking service, heat exchanger tube inspection, and PAUT or TOFD where cracks need sizing. Findings go to the owner's inspector on the same shift, with a daily summary of items completed, findings raised and items blocked by access, so the planners can re-sequence work while there is still time.

Repairs and emergent work

When a finding leads to a repair, the repair welds need their own examination: visual, MT or PT on root and final passes, and RT or UT where the code calls for volumetric examination. Keeping the same crew on site for repair NDE avoids a second mobilisation and keeps the records in one place.

Can NDT be performed during a shutdown or turnaround?

Yes, and most internal inspection can only be done then, because vessels, columns and exchanger bundles have to be opened, cleaned and gas-freed first. The better question is how much external work can be moved out of the outage. External UT thickness surveys, on-stream piping inspection and corrosion mapping can often be done in the weeks before shutdown, which shortens the outage scope and gives the planners early warning of repairs.

After the outage

The handover package carries the procedure, calibration and personnel records for every method, the findings with photographs and sketches, and the Level III review, ready for the owner's inspector to update the equipment records and set the next intervals. Atlantis NDT supports the owner's inspection programme, and your Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record. If findings should live with the equipment record rather than in a binder, see how our inspection software keeps them together. To plan an outage, send the work list and the dates.
